theorem_title: For a ℂ-subspace W ⊆ ℂⁿ, the orthogonal {z : w · z = 0 for all w ∈ W} for the bilinear dot product is a ℂ-subspace of dimension n − dim W
formal_statement:
open Complex ComplexConjugate

namespace DiazModulus

theorem fv_dot_orthogonal {n : ℕ} (W : Submodule ℂ (Fin n → ℂ)) :
    ∃ V : Submodule ℂ (Fin n → ℂ), (∀ z, z ∈ V ↔ ∀ w ∈ W, w ⬝ᵥ z = 0) ∧
      Module.finrank ℂ ↥V + Module.finrank ℂ ↥W = n := by
  sorry

end DiazModulus
natural_language_statement:
For $u, v \in \mathbb C^n$, $u \cdot v = \sum_k u_k v_k$ is the bilinear dot product (not the Hermitian one).

For every $\mathbb C$-subspace $W \subseteq \mathbb C^n$ there is a $\mathbb C$-subspace $V \subseteq \mathbb C^n$ with
$$V = \{z \in \mathbb C^n : w \cdot z = 0 \text{ for all } w \in W\} \quad\text{and}\quad \dim V + \dim W = n.$$
source: Classical linear algebra; a step of the proof of M. Waldschmidt, Further variations on the six exponentials theorem, Hardy-Ramanujan J. 28 (2005), 1–9, Th. 2.1 (pp. 5–6). Novelty: none claimed; routine. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 14 November 2026 (C. Perassi).
